biography: Thiago Camilo, a name whispered with both admiration and apprehension in Brazilian motorsport, hails from the bustling favelas of São Paulo. His journey began not on a racetrack, but on the chaotic streets, dodging traffic and navigating the urban maze on a battered scooter – skills that unknowingly honed his reflexes and spatial awareness. At 14, a local karting event offered a glimpse into a different world. Scrapping together funds, he entered and, against all odds, won, catching the eye of Kart 4. The team offered him a contract, and thus began his ascent. Though initially rough around the edges, his raw talent was undeniable. Now, at 21, after years with Ipiranga Racing, Camilo is a force to be reckoned with, his aggressive style making him a constant threat for podium finishes. He dreams of international stardom, fueled by the memory of his early struggles.
drivingStyle: Camilo's driving is best described as a controlled explosion. He attacks corners with unparalleled ferocity, often pushing the limits of adhesion. His tire management is improving, but it remains a work in progress, often sacrificing early-race pace for a late-race surge. Under pressure, Camilo thrives; the tighter the situation, the more focused and daring he becomes. He has an uncanny ability to sense the optimal moment to overtake, often executing maneuvers that leave his rivals dumbfounded.

rivalries.reason: A bitter rivalry stemming from a controversial collision at Interlagos that cost Vargas the championship. The two drivers have exchanged heated words and aggressive moves on the track ever since.
A clash of generations and driving styles. Flores, a seasoned veteran, views Camilo's aggressive tactics as reckless, while Camilo sees Flores as overly cautious and predictable.
Both drivers rose through the ranks together in karting and have been locked in a constant battle for supremacy ever since, each pushing the other to their absolute limit.

quirks: Always wears the same faded wristband he got when he won his first karting race.
Listens to a specific Brazilian samba song before every race to calm his nerves.
Refuses to start a race if his helmet isn't perfectly aligned.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about playing it safe; it's about pushing boundaries and taking risks. If you're not on the edge, you're taking up space."
careerHighlight: Winning the Stock Car Pro Series race at Curitiba in 2022 after starting from the back of the grid due to a qualifying penalty. He carved his way through the field with a series of daring overtakes, showcasing his raw talent and determination.
careerLowPoint: Spinning out of the lead on the final lap of the 2021 Cascavel race, handing the victory to his arch-rival, Ricardo Vargas. The mistake cost him valuable championship points and haunted him for months.
